stories.question: Why did Nvidia overtake Apple as the world's most valuable listed company on November 3, 2026?

time_basis.current_observation: Nvidia passed Apple as the world's most valuable listed company during U.S. trading on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, with values measured around midday New York time.

background_events.event: Apple guided its December-quarter gross margin, the share of sales left after direct product costs, to 45% to 46%, below the 46.3% analysts expected, citing higher memory costs and saying memory prices would keep rising after the holiday quarter.

stories.event_title: Nvidia Passes Apple as World's Most Valuable Company After Memory-Cost Warning
stories.surface_summary_text: Apple warned that rising memory-chip costs will narrow its December-quarter profit margin, pushing its stock down, while chip stocks rebounded and Nvidia's stock-market value moved above Apple's.
stories.what_happened_text: The Nasdaq 100 rose 0.7% to 28,184 on Tuesday as chipmakers rebounded, and Nvidia became the world's most valuable company. Apple had said its December-quarter gross margin, the share of sales left after direct product costs, would be 45% to 46%, below the 46.3% forecast, because memory chips cost more. Apple shares fell 2.2% to $330.97, removing about $107 billion of stock-market value. Nvidia shares rose 2.9% to $207.95, ending a four-session losing streak and adding about $142 billion. At midday, Nvidia was worth $5.01 trillion and Apple was worth $4.83 trillion, leaving Nvidia about $181 billion ahead. Apple had ended Monday about $68 billion ahead.
stories.why_happened_text: Higher memory-chip prices raise Apple's costs per device, so investors sold Apple shares. The same price increases benefit chip suppliers, and chip stocks rebounded. Nvidia, a large chip company, gained with the group after four down sessions. Apple's drop and Nvidia's rise together moved Nvidia's stock-market value above Apple's.
stories.affected_assets_summary_text: The rebound went beyond Nvidia: the VanEck Semiconductor ETF gained 2.3%, and the Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund rose 1.3%.

market_summary.summary_text: Apple warned that more expensive memory chips will cut its December-quarter profit margin, and the stock fell 2.2%, while chip stocks rallied and Nvidia rose 2.9%. At midday, Nvidia became the world's most valuable listed company with a stock-market value of $5.01 trillion, about $181 billion above Apple's $4.83 trillion. The Nasdaq 100 rose 0.7% on the semiconductor rebound, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.4% as Apple declined. The move shows that higher memory prices transfer profit from device makers to chip suppliers.
limitations: Market values and prices are intraday snapshots from around midday Eastern time on November 3, 2026; the source report was published before the close and did not verify final closing values.
The explanation that rising memory-chip costs hurt Apple and helped chip stocks is the source's stated interpretation; other demand or cost factors may also have moved individual shares.
